epic.title: Static site: analyst-grade benchmark report, fast and accessible

features.title: Learn pages: how it works, methodology and caveats, add a model

tasks.title: Write the Add a question learner page
tasks.description: Mirror the existing Add a model page with a new /learn/add-a-question/ page that walks a contributor through the questions.json schema (subjects, framings, claims, tagline), shows a worked example diff, and links directly to the new pull request template so someone proposing a new benchmark question has an equally clear, code-free on-ramp as someone proposing a model.
acceptanceCriteria: Page lives at /learn/add-a-question/ and is reachable from the Learn section navigation
Documents each questions.json field (id, subjects, framings, claims, tagline) with a worked example diff
Links to the pull request template added for question/model contributions
Passes axe accessibility checks and the responsive audit like every other page

matchedItem.title: Write the Add a model page

duplicateReason.explanation: Matches completed task "Write the Add a model page".

epic.title: Fork this: make spinning up your own cross-model analysis a five-minute path

features.title: CONTRIBUTING sections and issue templates for adding a provider, a model, and a question

tasks.title: Add a GitHub pull request template for question and model contributions
tasks.description: The repo has issue templates for proposing a provider, model, or question, but no PR template steering the actual code change. Add a scoped PR template with a checklist (questions.json or models.json diff, mock-mode fixture added, npm run validate and npm test passing, screenshot of the new question/model rendering) so a contributor's first PR converges quickly during review.
acceptanceCriteria: .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/ contains a template selectable for adding a question or model, or the default template gains a clearly labeled section for it
Checklist includes registry file diff, mock fixture, npm run validate, npm test, and a rendered screenshot
Template links to the Add a question learner page and CONTRIBUTING.md
Referenced from CONTRIBUTING.md so a contributor finds it before opening a PR

epic.title: Community contribution pathway: on-site call-to-action for new questions and models (MVP)

features.title: Contribution call-to-action across the site
features.description: Surface the ability to propose a new question or model directly on the live site, not just in repo docs, so a reader who wonders why their question isn't included finds the path immediately. Scoped to messaging and links only; account creation, in-browser key entry, and self-service runs stay deferred to the existing Run your own benchmark epic.

tasks.title: Add a sitewide 'Propose a question or model' call-to-action
tasks.description: Add a persistent, no-JavaScript-required link (footer or masthead, matching the existing En Dash footer line pattern) that opens a prefilled GitHub issue for proposing a new benchmark question or model, so the ask is visible on every page rather than buried in docs.
acceptanceCriteria: CTA is present in the site footer (or equivalent persistent location) on every page, including with JavaScript disabled
Link opens a GitHub issue prefilled with the appropriate template and query parameters (title/labels)
CTA copy is sourced from the site copy registry per the project's registry-driven copy rule, not hardcoded to 'hot dog'
Passes the existing axe, responsive, and keyboard audits with the new element included

tasks.title: Add contribution messaging to the reports landing and history pages
tasks.description: Explain, in the report and history pages themselves, that the question set grows through community-submitted PRs, and link to the new Add a question learner page and the sitewide CTA. This is the primary place a reader forms the 'I have a question idea' impulse, so the explanation belongs there, not only on a dedicated learn page.
acceptanceCriteria: Reports landing page and /history/ page each carry a short paragraph or callout explaining how new questions get added, sourced from the copy registry
Callout links to /learn/add-a-question/ and the GitHub PR template
Copy renders correctly for a forked instance asking a different question, with no hardcoded 'hot dog' text outside questions.json
Passes npm run validate and the axe/responsive suites
